panels.description: Wide, full page width. Dusk over Padmini Amma's estate: a Kerala house of steep, low-swooping tiled roofs behind a gatehouse. A servant moves along the front courtyard lighting small oil lamps in the wall niches, one by one. Two palanquins set down just inside the gate. A small troop of Nair household guards in white, swords and round shields, stays at the gate with their eyes on the road and the perimeter. Road dust still hangs in the last light. No elephants, no drums.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The King came to Padmini Amma's estate not with the thunder of drums or the announcement of heralds, but with the quiet dust of a traveller who knows the road too well.

panels.description: Medium. Marthanda Varma (V13 sheet, cream and gold, no spear on this visit, bare-headed, his hair in a side knot above his left ear, no turban, no crest) stepping down from the plainer palanquin, already moving, coiled. Behind him, from a second and more ornate palanquin, the Senior Rani: very upright, the same bearing as his, hair pulled back severely with no flowers, white with a narrow gold border. At her side the Prince, about ten, in a small white mundu with a thin gold chain and a small neat topknot, very still, eyes wide and watchful.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: His sister, the Senior Rani of Attingal. Her son. The heir.

panels.description: Padmini Amma on the front verandah above the steps: in her fifties, her finest white cotton, fresh jasmine in her coiled black hair, one simple gold chain, her long walking stick in hand. Her face set in lines of old iron. She is looking off-panel, across the courtyard.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Stay.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: This is not a state visit. It is a family matter.

panels.description: Nagoji under the jackfruit tree at the edge of the courtyard, caught half-turned, one bare foot already on the side path. Deep shade under the leaves.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I am not family, Amma. I should leave.

panels.description: Narrow strip. Padmini, unmoving, not raising her voice. A newly lit lamp in the niche behind her.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: You will stay.

panels.description: The King on the verandah steps, bent low, his fingers touching Padmini's feet. She looks down at him, softened. Far in the background, Nagoji under the tree, seeing it.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Valiyamma.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had rarely seen him show that reverence to anyone. Even priests.

panels.description: Padmini (jasmine) lifting her gaze past the King to the Rani (no jasmine) and the Prince coming up the steps.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Highness. And the future.

copy.speaker: RANI
copy.text: The past remembers the debt, Padmini Amma. We have brought the boy to see the walls that saved his uncle.

panels.description: The Prince, close, in his small white mundu and thin gold chain. His uncle's sharp cheekbones, his mother's watchful stillness. His eyes have stopped on Nagoji, who has come nearer.

copy.speaker: PRINCE
copy.text: You are the Maratha. The one who trains horses to dance with muskets.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I am.

panels.description: Two-shot from low: the boy looking up, Nagoji looking down, perfectly serious with him.

copy.speaker: PRINCE
copy.text: My uncle says you once killed three men in Goa with a chain still on your wrist.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Your uncle exaggerates. It was two men.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The third I only broke.

panels.description: Full width. The boy weighing this with total gravity. Behind him the King is hiding his amusement. The Rani's hand is moving toward her son's shoulder.

copy.speaker: PRINCE
copy.text: I would like to learn how to break men.

copy.speaker: PRINCE
copy.text: When I am older.

panels.description: The Rani's hand settled on the boy's shoulder. She speaks to him, but her eyes are on Nagoji.

copy.speaker: RANI
copy.text: You will learn many things when you are older. For now, you will learn to watch and remember.

copy.speaker: RANI
copy.text: That is what kings do before they act.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The same cold counting that lived in her brother.

panels.description: The Rani and Nagoji face to face. Cool, measured, unhurried.

copy.speaker: RANI
copy.text: My brother trusts you. I am slower to trust. But I am told you have kept him alive when others would have let him fall.

copy.speaker: RANI
copy.text: That buys you my attention, if not yet my confidence.

panels.description: Nagoji inclines his head. The Rani is already turning toward the inner doorway.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I ask for nothing more, Highness.

copy.speaker: RANI
copy.text: Good. Men who ask for too much too quickly tend to lose what they already have.

panels.description: Large, half the page. The *nalukettu* from a high corner: a square of open evening sky above a sunken stone court, steep gabled roofs swooping low on four sides. Dark teak pillars at the corners, carved with yalis and processions of elephants that seem to march around the wood carrying the roof. A black oxide floor polished to a dark mirror, holding the lamps' reflections. On one side of the court, an open doorway into a dim storeroom. The King on a low wooden stool, the Prince beside him copying his posture exactly. The Rani (no jasmine), standing very upright. Padmini (jasmine), seated, her walking stick leaning beside her. Ramayyan (thin, receding hair, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundle) half in shadow. Nagoji standing apart at the edge of the light.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Ramayyan had arrived without a sound, as always.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I was an intruder in a shrine.

panels.description: The King on his stool, the Prince beside him mirroring him. The King looking up at Nagoji, amused.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Sit.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Nagoji Sawant. You look ready to jump over the wall.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Royal visits usually involve more warning, Highness. And fewer secrets.

panels.description: The King's eyes roaming the carved pillars and the dark timber ceiling. Behind him, Nagoji glances at Padmini, who is watching the King with affection and fierce protectiveness.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: This house has held bigger secrets than this.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Do you know why I trust Valiyamma more than my own ministers? Why her grain wagons pass my checkpoints without being searched?

panels.description: The King's arm and pointing finger in the foreground. At the end of it, across the courtyard and through the open doorway, the dim storeroom beyond: clay rice vessels taller than a man's waist, and in its far corner a small, low wooden door that looks like nothing more than a repair panel, barely visible.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: That leads to the cellar. Beneath the granary. Dark, full of spiders and the smell of old rice.

panels.description: Flashback. The same cellar, thirty years earlier: an earth-walled hollow under low beams, straw-bound paddy bundles and clay grain jars, a woven mat. Young Varma, about seven and gaunt, in a torn, grimy dark-brown waist-cloth, matted uncut hair, no gold, crouched between the jars in near-dark, knees drawn up, eyes huge. Cobwebs. Thin slits of light through the plank floor overhead.

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: Thirty years ago I was not yet eight years old, but I was a hunted animal.

panels.description: Flashback strip: three separate narrow slivers side by side, each generated separately and composited (as in ch13 15.3). Left: a bowl of rice pushed away untouched on a mat. Centre: small gold coins (fanams) pressed into a palace guard's palm. Right: a figure with a drawn blade waiting on a moonlit road.

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: The Lords of the Eight Houses, the Ettuveetil Pillamar, wanted my blood.

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: I could trust no one. Not the palace, not the temples.

panels.description: Flashback, looking up from below. The storeroom's plank floor overhead, slits of lamplight, the shadows of feet crossing. Dust sifting down onto young Varma's upturned face. Both his hands are pressed over his mouth.

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: I lived there for three weeks. I heard their boots on the floorboards above my head.

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: I heard them threaten Valiyamma.

panels.description: Flashback, above: the storeroom over the cellar, a plank floor, clay rice vessels, a wooden post, one torch. Armed retainers of the Pillamar with swords and round shields, one holding the torch. Their leader: older, gold earrings, sword drawn. One retainer holds a knife flat against the throat of Padmini's husband, an unarmed, bare-chested Nair man in a plain mundu, pinned against the post; no blood. Young Padmini (Padmini's face at about twenty-five, black hair coiled at the nape, plain white) stepping forward toward the leader, composed and empty-handed. Behind her, through a doorway, a cloth cradle hung from a beam with a swaddled infant asleep in it. No cup anywhere in this panel.

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: I heard them hold a knife to her husband's throat.

panels.description: Present. The Prince's eyes wide. The King turning his gaze to Padmini.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: And what did she do?

panels.description: Padmini, close, dry as old rice. Small flashback inset in the lower corner (muted palette, soft border): young Padmini's hand holding out a brass cup of buttermilk to the Pillamar leader.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: I offered them buttermilk.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: And told them that if they woke my baby, I would curse their lineage for seven generations.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: They were superstitious men. They left.

panels.description: Full width. The King smiling, and the smile does not reach his eyes. Padmini watching him.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: She hid me when I was hunted. She risked her house, her life, and her child for a prince who was fourth in line and had nothing to give her but promises.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: You have kept those promises.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Not all of them.

panels.description: Padmini, very still. Behind her and out of focus, Nagoji, his hand stopped halfway to his sash, his head only starting to turn.

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: I am here to offer you a son.

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: Not as a replacement for your son and husband, felled by the Pillamar's men,

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: but as a new staff for my Valiyamma to lean on in her old age.

panels.description: The King turning on his stool to face Nagoji. The playfulness is gone.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Nagoji Sawant. You have commanded my horse. You have built my walls. You have bled at Colachel.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You serve me better than men who share my blood.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I serve the hand that feeds me.

panels.description: Ramayyan at the edge of the lamplight, arms folded over his palm-leaf bundle.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: That is a mercenary's answer. The King needs more than a mercenary.

panels.description: The King leaning forward, elbows on knees. The Prince beside him leans forward too. Between the King and Nagoji, a thread of smoke from a floor lamp drifts sideways across the frame toward Nagoji.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You are a stranger here. A man with no clan, no *tharavadu* to claim him.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: In Travancore, a man without a house is like smoke. He drifts with the wind.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I cannot have my best cavalry commander drift.

panels.description: Ramayyan holding out a single rolled palm leaf, a royal ola writ, bound with saffron thread (no visible script). The King does not take it. He looks at Nagoji over it, dry.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: The priests say a man's caste is written in bone.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: But I have found that even the gods' writing can be edited, if the ink is gold.

panels.description: Close on the King, eyes glittering. Beside him, Ramayyan's fingers loosening the saffron thread on the rolled leaf.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: The Chief Priest has discovered, after a surprisingly generous donation to the temple roof fund, that your lineage was not Maratha after all, but a lost branch of a Nair house that wandered north.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: A miracle.

panels.description: Wide. The Rani (no jasmine) stepping forward holding a silver plate: a folded cloth, a small lit lamp, and a little ivory elephant with a gold-tipped tusk. The King, formal now, addressing Padmini (jasmine), who is seated. Everyone else frozen in place.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: I formally request that the House of Padmini Amma accept a new son. Not of blood, but of water and oath.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: That he be given the rights of the hearth, the protection of the name, and the duty of the lineage.

directions: Lettering note: both balloons in the formal court register (a finer face or a double-ruled balloon), since the King has switched to the high Malayalam of the court.

panels.description: Nagoji's face, lamplit, holding very still. At the panel's edge, Padmini rising from her seat.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: This was no small thing. It meant inheriting the debts, the feuds, the ancestors.

panels.description: Padmini in front of him, both hands cupping his face. Her eyes on Nagoji; her words aimed at the King off-panel, the balloon tails running back toward him. Her voice is not quite steady.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: He eats too much. And he cleans his sword in the house, which annoys the servants.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: And he broods like an old woman when it rains.

panels.description: Insert, tight. Her work-rough hands turning his left wrist upward, his cream tunic sleeve pushed back to the forearm. The Portuguese brand on the inner LEFT wrist: a pale, ridged scar (draw raised ridges only, no legible letters). His nails healed but ridged. Her thumb tracing the scar.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: This mark says you belong to men who wanted to break you. It says you are property.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: It says you are less than the goats they slaughtered for their feasts.

panels.description: Padmini's face, close. Her grip tightening on his wrist.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: But this house says otherwise. This house says you are mine.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: And no brand, no empire, no company of merchants will ever own what I have claimed.

panels.description: Large, full width, the tallest panel on the page. Padmini presses her lips to the scar on his inner left wrist, swift and fierce. Nagoji caught in the act of almost pulling away. The black floor mirrors them both. Hold it.
She raises her head. Eyes wet, face iron. She is already turning toward the King.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: You are already my son in every way that matters to the gods. The only thing left is to tell the gods formally.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: I accept.

panels.description: The Rani (no jasmine) dips a fingertip in the oil of the lamp on the silver plate and touches it to Nagoji's forehead. Nagoji has bared his head to receive it: the rust-red turban is off and folded in his hands, his long curly hair loose. The Prince stands next to him, face tilted up to receive his. Padmini (jasmine) at Nagoji's shoulder. A touch of oil, not a painted mark.

copy.speaker: RANI
copy.text: Witness. This is how loyalty is woven.

copy.speaker: RANI
copy.text: Not just with gold, but with kinship.

panels.description: The King standing before Nagoji, who is bare-headed now, the folded turban in his hand. Nothing of the strategist or the warlord in the King's face.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For the first time I saw a man paying a debt he had carried for thirty years.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You are Nagoji of Padmini's House now. The stranger is gone. Do not let us find him again.

panels.description: Medium. Nagoji, bare-headed, the folded turban in his hand, his throat working. The King already turning away with one hand on the Prince's shoulder, his eyes on Padmini as he speaks.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I will not, Highness.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Good. Come.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Kings do not always sit on thrones. Sometimes they sit in the dark and wait for a woman with a sharp tongue to save them.

panels.description: Wide. Night. Background: across the courtyard, through the open doorway into the dim storeroom, the King holding the low cellar door open and beckoning; the Prince hesitating on its threshold. The Rani (no jasmine) at the storeroom doorway, pausing and glancing back toward Nagoji. High above, the latticed ventilation screens let in moonlight that throws geometric shadows across the black floor. Foreground: Padmini (jasmine), her hand resting on Nagoji's forearm, looking up at him.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: A name. You need one that fits this house.

copy.speaker: RANI (from the doorway)
copy.text: In this land, a man belongs to his mother's line. You have no mother here. But you have Valiyamma.

panels.description: Padmini, after a silence, giving it to him. Behind them in the shadows, Ramayyan, stylus already poised over a palm leaf.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Ananthan. For the serpent on which Lord Padmanabha rests.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: The one who holds up the world without asking for thanks.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Ananthan Pillai. It will do. The records will reflect it.

panels.description: The Prince coming back out of the storeroom first, eyes wide, dust on his knees. The King behind him, one hand on the boy's shoulder, the other holding out a small bundle wrapped in red cloth.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Ananthan Pillai. Now you look like you belong.

panels.description: The bundle open in Nagoji's palm, the red cloth falling away, a plain dark wooden sheath beside it. A straight dagger catching the lamplight: the blade about a hand-span long, the whole knife no longer than his forearm, an ivory grip with gold fittings at guard and pommel.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Dutch steel, taken off my beach and hammered into something worth carrying.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: If you must wear a foreigner's iron at your belt, let it carry my sign.

panels.description: Inset, tight, in the lower corner of 12.2. A small right-spiralling conch outline struck into the steel near the hilt, plain and unlettered. His fingers closing around the ivory.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: This is too much.

copy.speaker: VARMA (off)
copy.text: It is exactly enough. A name ties you to a house. A blade ties you to a duty.

panels.description: Wide. Night. The same courtyard, emptied. The lamps burned low, the black floor holding their last reflections. Nagoji alone beside a carved pillar, still in tunic and sash, the rust-red turban folded on the floor at his feet. His arms are raised: he is gathering his long curly hair into a knot high on his crown for the first time. The new knife in its dark wooden sheath at his sash.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had ridden into this land as Nagoji Sawant, on a borrowed horse, branded by enemies, carrying nothing but the memory of a drowned friend and a war I could not finish.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I would stay as Ananthan Pillai.

panels.description: Close. His fingertips on the carved procession of elephants climbing the pillar, trunk to tail, in the last of the lamplight.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They marched trunk to tail, carrying nothing, going nowhere, holding up the roof simply because that was what they had been made to do.

panels.description: Tight, at hip height. The conch knife's ivory hilt in its dark sheath at his sash, and beside it his fingertips still resting on the carved elephants of the pillar.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The knife's weight pressed at my waist, its conch a second mark against my skin.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I understood then what the King had given and what he expected in return.

panels.description: His face in the last lamplight, the new knot on his crown, turned up toward the elephants as they climb the pillar into the dark of the roof.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I understood them now.

panels.description: Day. Rain pouring in sheets off the eaves of the front verandah. Nagoji seated at the verandah's edge watching it. Revathi arriving under the eaves, her hair rain-damp.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Three days later.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Ananthan Pillai. It suits you less than I expected.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: It will grow into me. Or I into it.

panels.description: She sits beside him, close enough that their shoulders almost touch. The rain hangs like a curtain between them and the world.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You have a house now. A name. A mother who will fight tigers for you.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: The stranger is gone.

panels.description: Nagoji, eyes on the rain. Revathi watching his profile.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The stranger was always a story I told myself. A way to keep one foot outside the door. In case I needed to run.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: And now?

panels.description: He turns to look at her. Droplets on her skin like scattered pearls.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Now I have a door of my own. And I would like you to come through it.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: That is bold, for a man who once told me he made no promises.

panels.description: He stands and holds out his hand. She looks at it and does not yet take it.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I am not making a promise. I am making an invitation.

panels.description: Her eyes going past him to the house: the carved pillars, the dark doorways. His hand still held out.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Padmini...

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Has gone to the temple.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The servants know better than to disturb the son of the house when he is entertaining.

panels.description: A smile tugging at the corner of her mouth. Her hand now in his.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You have grown arrogant very quickly, Ananthan Pillai.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I have grown certain. There is a difference.

panels.description: Wide and low. The dim storeroom, grey rain-light from the doorway behind them: clay rice vessels taller than a man's waist. He leads her by the hand between them. In the far corner, the same low wooden door from page 4, like a repair panel, waiting.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The cellar door no longer felt like a secret I was borrowing.

panels.description: The cellar. He sets down a lamp he has just lit; its glow finds earth walls, low beams, clay grain jars, straw-bound paddy bundles and a woven mat. Revathi at the foot of the steps.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: The last time, I brought you here.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: The last time, I had nothing to offer but myself. Now I have walls. A roof. A name that will not wash away with the next tide.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You think that matters to me?

panels.description: Close two-shot in lamplight, faces near. Her eyes searching his face.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I think you have spent years being the one who decides. The one who comes and goes. The one who holds the door.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Tonight, let me hold it.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: She did not find it.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: One night. Then we see.

panels.description: The embrace, shown by the lamp: their two shadows thrown tall on the earth wall and merging into one. The couple themselves small and half-lost in the dark below, both fully clothed; only the merged shadows show the embrace.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: We both knew it was a lie.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I was a man in his own house, with a woman who had chosen to enter it.

panels.description: Afterward. The lamp low. Frame at the shoulders, as in ch16 11.1: they lie on the mat under a cotton cloth drawn up to the shoulders, her sari drawn around her under the cloth, her head on his chest. Her fingertip tracing the brand on the inner LEFT wrist of his raised hand.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The mark that no longer felt like a chain.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: The man who washed up on this coast would not have taken my hand. He would have waited for me to take his.

panels.description: Still framed at the shoulders. Nagoji, eyes on the low beams. Revathi propped on one elbow to look at him, the cloth held to her shoulder.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: He had nothing to offer.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: He had himself. That was always enough. He just did not know it.

panels.description: Revathi, dressed, at the top of the cellar steps, one hand on the open door, looking back down at him. Beyond her the storeroom is dark: night has come and the rain has stopped, a thin blue of moonlight on the clay vessels. In the foreground, the lamp guttering.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: I will come again. Not because you have a house now, but because you finally believe you deserve one.

panels.description: Full width, the last panel. The door above is shut, a hairline of moonlight at its edges. The lamp in the foreground: the wick gone dark, a single thread of smoke rising. Beyond it, Nagoji lies on the mat in near-darkness, eyes open, looking up at the low beams.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For the first time, the walls around me were not a cage but a foundation.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Some debts are paid by becoming what is needed, and learning to call it home.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: And some doors, once opened, are never fully closed again.

frames.review_note: Minor, retouch if possible: the two palanquins seen through the gate stand on small wheels under their carrying poles (about x 0.22-0.30, y 0.75-0.82). Palanquins are carried, and in 1.2 and 1.5 they rest on legs. The guards carry spears as well as their swords and round shields. Otherwise clean: dusk estate, gatehouse, Nair guards watching the road, a servant lighting wall-niche lamps, road dust and the jackfruit tree. No text. The wide quiet dusk sky across the top has room for the long caption.

Varma's hair knot sits at the back of his crown, not the bible's side knot above the LEFT ear. Otherwise he follows the private-visit look: bare-headed, no turban, crest or spear, the V13 face and moustache, gold necklaces, a cream and gold mundu. He also has a gold-bordered shoulder cloth. The Rani matches her sheet: severe bun with no flowers, white sari with a narrow gold border, gold ear studs. The Prince, about ten, wears a white mundu, a thin gold chain and a small topknot. Ornate and plainer palanquins rest on legs, which is right. The sky above the gate at the upper left has room for the caption.

Minor background details: three palanquins appear beyond the gate opening rather than two just inside it, and Padmini shows little grey threading. Otherwise clean. Padmini matches her sheet and stands on the verandah above the steps: old Kerala drape with no blouse, a white and gold sari, jasmine in her hair, a gold chain, walking stick in hand. She has a set face and looks off-panel left across the courtyard. The open dusk sky between the jackfruit tree and the roof has room for both balloons.

Minor background-only issues: the two palanquins beyond the gateway look like they sit on small wheels rather than being set down on their poles, and the gate guards hold spears with their round shields rather than swords. Both are small, far back, and do not affect the beat.
